raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several language model variants. The x-axis represents the number of iterations (#Iteration), displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents Loss on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration. The purple line labeled "Vanilla" starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations, then gradually levels off, reaching approximately 2.50 by iteration 140,000, placing it among the lowest final loss values. The blue line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)" follows a similar initial steep decline but converges to a higher loss of approximately 2.62 by iteration 140,000, remaining consistently above most other lines throughout training. The orange line labeled "SepLLM (n=64)" starts similarly high and decreases to approximately 2.52 by iteration 140,000, closely tracking the Vanilla line. The green line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)" follows a nearly identical trajectory to the orange line, ending at approximately 2.52. The red line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" also follows a very similar path, ending at approximately 2.51 by iteration 140,000. The dark blue line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)" decreases to approximately 2.53 by iteration 140,000, tracking closely with the other SepLLM variants. All lines exhibit shaded regions around them indicating variance or confidence intervals. The StrmLLM (n=64) line is notably separated above the cluster of Vanilla and SepLLM variants throughout most of the training, while the Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) lines are tightly grouped together at the lower end of the loss range.
